article_content: On November 28, 2012, a stunning 300lb gingerbread replica of the White House was revealed as the highlight of the White House Christmas decorations by Michelle Obama. This elaborate structure, featuring a marzipan version of the kitchen garden and a large model of First Dog Bo, was prominently displayed in the State Dining Room. Dressed in a gold Michael Kors outfit, the First Lady unveiled the decorations to an appreciative audience of military families and later engaged in holiday crafts with the children. The theme for this year's decorations was 'Joy to All', but Bo, the First Dog, seemed to steal the spotlight. There were 40 'Bo-flake' ornaments scattered throughout the White House, showcasing cutout images of the dog. A life-size replica of Bo, complete with a string of lights in his mouth, was placed in the East Garden Room. Additionally, an oversized statue of the Portuguese water dog stood next to the 300-pound gingerbread house in the State Dining Room. Mrs. Obama highlighted Bo's significance at the White House, stating, 'He's almost as big as the house. He is such a huge personality.' Visitors also received a Bo bookmark that guided them on a scavenger hunt for 'Bo-ornaments' hidden in eight rooms. Bo himself made an appearance, wearing a jingle bell collar, and was quickly surrounded by eager young guests. This year's decorations included many handmade items that could easily be replicated at home, such as patriotic wreaths and ornaments wrapped in red, white, and blue yarn, aligning with Mrs. Obama's emphasis on supporting military families. The gargantuan gingerbread house, however, was not a simple task. It contained over 175 pounds of gingerbread and more than 50 pounds of chocolate. Pastry chef Bill Yosses created a blend of wheat, rye, and white-flour gingerbread to mimic the color of the sandstone house before it was first painted white in 1798. More than 90,000 visitors were expected to tour the White House during the holiday season. Executive chef Cristeta Comerford planned to use recipes from Mrs. Obama's gardening book, 'American Grown', to prepare food for the guests, including sweet potato quick bread, green beans with almonds, and a winter salad featuring fennel. The massive decorating effort, involving 54 live Christmas trees, was completed in just five days with the help of 85 volunteers from across the country.

article_content: At the end of Arsenal's 1-0 win over Southampton on Wednesday, the spotlight focused on Arsene Wenger's strikeforce. How can he get Danny Welbeck to improve after missing a host of chances against the Saints? How much longer can he rely on Alexis Sanchez to get Arsenal out of trouble? Should he bring Thierry Henry to the club as a coach, passing on his expertise, as soon as possible? Everyone, it seemed, had forgotten about one of the World Cup winners missing from Arsenal's ranks. Mesut Ozil watched Arsenal beat Southampton and gave his approval of the result by saying 'job well done.' Mesut Ozil (center) in action for Arsenal against Tottenham earlier in the Premier League season. Alexis Sanchez (right) fires past Fraser Forster (center) of Southampton to win all three points for Arsenal. But playmaker Mesut Ozil watched his team break down Ronald Koeman's side, and while the performance had plenty of room for improvement, the result got his seal of approval. 'Job well done,' he said, alongside a picture of him watching the game wrapped up in a blanket as winter sets in across England. Ozil was ruled out of action for 12 weeks with a knee injury at the start of October, and Arsenal will no doubt be hoping he can return to top form when he returns in the new year.

Mesut Ozil vio al Arsenal vencer al Southampton y dio su aprobación al resultado diciendo 'trabajo bien hecho.' Ozil fue descartado de la acción durante 12 semanas por una lesión en la rodilla a principios de octubre, y el Arsenal sin duda espera que pueda volver a su mejor forma cuando regrese en el nuevo año.

article_content: MailOnline exclusively revealed that the couple will wed in the Florentine landmark Forte Belvedere. They paid $410,000 to rent the venue for May 24, according to the city's mayor. Rapper Kanye West has been staying in the Italian city ahead of the nuptials without Kim. Reality star Kim Kardashian is back in LA after a brief visit to New York for an E! appearance. For months, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West looked set to exchange vows in France, even listing Paris as the wedding destination on their invite. But after it emerged this week that the couple will actually say 'I do' in Florence, the rapper has revealed why the Italian city is so close to their hearts. In an interview with Florence's La Nazione newspaper on Friday, the 36-year-old said: 'I adore Florence. I love Italy and the Italian lifestyle. To tell you the truth, I already came to the banks of the Arno [river] with Kim last year, just the two of us, incognito.' He continued: 'I think that our daughter North was conceived here among the Renaissance masterpieces. It was our first honeymoon. It is one of the most beautiful cities in the world—for me the most beautiful in Europe.' The groom made it clear he is feeling giddy ahead of the big day. 'I am very happy,' he said. 'I am a romantic: for Mother’s Day I gave Kim a wall of flowers. Family is everything for me, the antidote to the pressure of fame. Family and creativity relax me. I am happy to create for my family.' West has been staying in Florence and quietly studying with fashion designer Ermanno Daelli, who is one owner of the fashion house Ermanno Scervino. He said Kim, 33, inspires him and said they turn to each other for fashion advice. 'I consult her on elegance and what I wear,' he revealed. 'And she does the same for me. Today as a musician I like to dress in a less showy way than in the past.' He is working on his music too, adding: 'I am composing a whole album, Made in Florence.' MailOnline exclusively revealed on Friday that the pair's fairytale wedding will take place at a sixteenth-century castle in Florence, with a dark history. The pair will marry next weekend in front of 1000 guests at the famous Florentine landmark Forte Belvedere, Scervino confirmed. The venue, a fortress built for the ruling Medici family of Florence, is a spectacular setting for their nuptials. The venue has a tragic past, however. Two young people fell from the ramparts in 2006 and 2008, prompting the authorities to close the venue. The couple rented the fort, located next to Florence's famed Boboli Gardens, for 300,000 euros ($410,000) and a Protestant minister will preside over the ceremony, a spokeswoman for Florence mayor's office said Friday. Kanye proposed to the reality star on her 33rd birthday in October 2013, renting out San Francisco's AT&T Park for the occasion. This is the first marriage for West, who was previously engaged to designer Alexis Phifer. It's the third trip down the aisle for Kardashian. She was wed to music producer Damon Thomas from 2000 to 2003, and spent 72 days married to professional basketball player Kris Humphries in 2011 after tying the knot in a lavish ceremony broadcast as a two-part TV special. The couple was featured on the cover of Vogue magazine's April issue, with Kardashian wearing a wedding-style dress.

article_content: Most parents would be overjoyed if their 11-year-old son was always laughing and smiling. However, for Rachel Martin, the mother of James Edgar, his perpetually cheerful demeanor serves as a constant reminder of the obstacles he faces. James was born with Angelman syndrome, a chromosomal disorder that results in severe learning difficulties. This rare neurological condition often leaves sufferers in a state of constant excitement, characterized by almost permanent laughter and smiling. Despite appearing to be one of the happiest children, James, who hails from Caernarfon, North Wales, grapples with intellectual and developmental delays, seizures, and jerky movements. There are fewer than 1,000 reported cases of Angelman syndrome in the UK. Rachel Martin describes her son as a 'happy, lovable, cuddly child' who requires constant supervision due to his lack of danger awareness. Though he may seem perpetually happy, he experiences a range of emotions, even if he doesn't outwardly display them. Rachel acknowledges that while James can be challenging at times, he brings immense joy to those around him. Although James cannot speak, he communicates effectively through his iPad, using various apps to share stories with his family and friends. Diagnosed at 17 months due to his delayed development, Rachel recalls the emotional turmoil of receiving the diagnosis. The realization that James had a disability instantly altered their future plans and expectations. Rachel highlights the transformative impact of the iPad on James's life, enabling him to communicate and engage with his favorite content, such as Disney parades and videos on YouTube. Despite the challenges, Rachel cherishes James for who he is and wouldn't change him. James lives with his siblings Alexandria, Zac, and Beth, who are very supportive. Rachel chairs the Angelman Syndrome Support Education and Research Trust, providing a support network for families affected by the syndrome. The Newlife Foundation is currently fundraising to provide James with a specialist bed to manage his complex behaviors, aiming to raise £5,000 in addition to the £2,500 already donated. For more information, visit www.newlifecharity.co.uk. Angelman Syndrome, first identified in 1965 by Dr. Harry Angelman, was initially called 'Happy Puppet Syndrome' due to the characteristic happy demeanor and jerky movements of affected children. It is a neurological disorder causing severe learning difficulties, with most children diagnosed between the ages of three and seven. For more information, visit www.angelmanuk.org/angelman_syndrome.html.

article_content: By Lauren Paxman. Last updated at 5:41 PM on 16th November 2011. Casualty departments are undergoing a 'calming' overhaul to reduce patient aggression towards staff. Measures include clearer information on waiting times, treatment processes, and refurbished waiting rooms to alleviate anxiety in these busy hospital areas. This initiative follows a rise in attacks on Health Service workers, with almost 60,000 assaults on NHS staff in England reported during 2010-11. Designers, psychologists, and healthcare experts were commissioned to develop innovative ways to keep patients calm and protect NHS workers. New features may include bus stop-style screens with live updates on waiting times. A Department of Health spokeswoman confirmed the involvement of these experts in the year-long project led by the Design Council. The project identified methods to ease patients' frustration and help them understand waiting times. Patients can expect to see live update screens detailing the number and types of cases being handled, along with clear signs and maps explaining treatment stages. A new approach to greeting patients in emergency units has also been suggested. Managers planning refurbishments will receive specific advice on lighting, decor, and seating. These suggestions will be tested in three NHS Foundation Trusts: Chesterfield Royal Hospital, University Hospital Southampton, and Guy's and St Thomas' in London. Attacks on NHS staff cost at least £69 million a year, according to the spokeswoman. Figures published last week revealed 57,830 assaults on doctors, nurses, paramedics, and ambulance crews in England during 2010/11 – an increase of 1,112 compared to the previous year. Nearly 70% of these attacks involved patients not responsible for their actions due to medical conditions, adverse reactions to treatment, mental health problems, or severe learning difficulties. Fewer than one in 40 attacks resulted in prosecution. Health Minister Simon Burns stated that any violence towards staff is 'totally unacceptable'. 'NHS staff work hard to save lives every day and should be able to do so without fear of assault,' he said. 'We want to safeguard staff and patients, which is why we asked the Design Council to help make A&E departments calmer and safer.' Dr Peter Carter, chief executive of the Royal College of Nursing, expressed concern that attacks could increase further if NHS budget cutbacks affect services. 'I am appalled by the nearly 58,000 physical assaults against our hardworking NHS staff this year. One assault is too many,' he said. 'Assaults on staff are never justified, but the worry is that if pressures increase and people wait longer, frustration levels will rise.' Christina McAnea, head of health at the Unison union, called the increase in violence a 'national disgrace' and urged immediate action to protect staff.

article_content: Algeria secured their spot in the Africa Cup of Nations quarter-finals with a decisive win over Senegal, thanks to goals from Riyad Mahrez and Nabil Bentaleb. Meanwhile, Ghana's late comeback against South Africa ensured Senegal's exit from the tournament, despite starting the day at the top of their group. Although Algeria finished second, their final match showcased a significant improvement in performance, highlighted by Bentaleb's spectacular goal. The Algerian squad celebrated as Bentaleb scored the second goal with a powerful shot from outside the box, sealing the victory and thrilling their fans. Algeria, known as the Desert Foxes, handled Senegal's aggressive play better than other teams in the tournament. Senegal's long-ball strategy proved ineffective, especially after their key player, Sadio Mane, was substituted with 25 minutes remaining. Both teams knew a win would secure a quarter-final spot, but a loss could mean elimination depending on the outcome in Mongomo. Algeria, needing a win more than Senegal, displayed greater intensity from the start. Within the first two minutes, Algeria nearly scored when Hila Soudani intercepted the ball and set up Sofiane Feghouli, who failed to capitalize on the opportunity. This set the tone for the match, with Senegal's defense struggling and Soudani causing constant trouble. Algeria took the lead on the 11th minute when Mahrez controlled a long pass and scored. Senegal tried to fight back but lacked finishing quality, with Mane and Mame Biram Diouf posing occasional threats. Their best chance came just before halftime, but Bentaleb made a crucial block. Even as Senegal pushed for an equalizer, Algeria looked more likely to score. A brilliant goal-line clearance and a missed chance by Mahrez didn't matter, as Bentaleb's stunning goal secured the win and Algeria's progress to the knockout stages.
